sections.value:
PASS-WITH-NOTES -- performance, round 1, PR #306
Head: be097a697256ffad0ad1a933706f0650342180f1

No performance blocker. No loop, poll, timer, hook or per-tick launch is added. The new native status read is demand-driven by an acknowledged canary, not multiplied by every live seat. The footer parser replaces an existing scan of the same captured text.

Cost and source audit

1. Catalog charge: the +1 omp.models launch is NOT limited to canaries whose chosen model source is the footer. governance.rs:2075-2092 calls observe_bind before native_runtime_model. adapter.rs:106-113 resolves any parsed OMP footer when native_session_id is present, even when native later wins. Therefore the incremental launch rate against today's broken parser is the rate of acknowledged, freshness-reaching OMP canaries with a recognized footer: +1 per such canary, including native-answered canaries. No canaries means zero additional launches/s, independent of idle fleet size. The only production daemon observe_bind caller is canary_command; bind's internal observe_bind supplies no native session id and cannot invoke the catalog.

2. The catalog site is existing, instrumented and unchanged apart from name matching: models.rs:316-360 records omp.models and calls program::launch("omp", ...) with ["models", "--json", "--no-extensions"]. It retains the existing five-second child timeout and ten-millisecond child-wait polling while this explicit operation runs; this is not a new fleet poll. The resolver normally launches the installed executable by its resolved path. The existing resolver's miss/relative-PATH fallback limits remain; the source-shape sensor is not runtime proof of absolute resolution or of child/grandchild counts. Catalog JSON is read and scanned per invocation; no cache or single-flight is introduced. Parallel canaries can incur parallel existing catalog operations.

3. Native read: one SessionStatusPort::status attempt per canary reaching model selection, across supported harnesses, with no child process. crates/unisphere/src/lib.rs:212-299 shares the existing per-seat cursor, serializes reads of one seat, preserves the cursor when callers stop waiting, and runs the fold on spawn_blocking. Warm append IO resumes at the saved offset; unchanged sources are statted rather than reread wholesale. A missing transcript is cached for 30 seconds; cold OMP lookup can walk configured session roots.

   This is incremental, NOT constant-bounded. Cold/reset reads fold the full transcript. The pinned SDK 0370cabbe4d9bcbb5b7bf6b0e13a490f0f4d0d59 (sdk/src/status.rs:600-727; sdk/src/prep.rs:135 onward) resumes from the cursor and drains input to its end. It caps a record/batch at 64 MiB, not the total transcript or the canary's status-read duration. Its warm result also clones small/bounded accumulators and scans retained recent-turn entries, so total CPU is not strictly just appended bytes. The canary directly awaits this read, without the card reader's separate wait bound. These are inherited SDK characteristics newly exercised by this on-demand caller, not an idle-fleet multiplier; no constant-time, hard-deadline or fixed-memory claim is made.

4. spawn_sites.rs scans harnesses production source and recognizes run_omp_command's Command::new plus spawns::record in the same function. The successful exact-head CI artifact contains passing every_daemon_launch_site_records_itself and no_daemon_launch_names_a_program_bare tests. No new daemon launch site is introduced. The new model_switch_pending projection is an O(1) field read, including existing card consumers.

CPU/RSS: /bin/ps -p 28181 -o pid=,lstart=,etime=,time=,%cpu=,rss= at both edges.

POST /v1/canary had no counter entry at either edge: zero recorded canary requests in the interval, and none recorded since this daemon started. omp.models was absent at both edges. Thus observed fleet canary rate was 0 / 20.213 s, not an assumed periodic frequency.

CPU time: 48.67 -> 52.48 s; +3.81 s / 20.213 s = 18.849% of one core. ps's separate instantaneous/smoothed %CPU field was 14.2 -> 11.0 and is not the interval calculation. RSS: 189600 -> 190432 KiB. Process start was Sat 21 Nov 11:33:24 2026 host local; daemon age was 02:04 -> 02:24, so this is a young-daemon baseline.

Machine probe: 20.0 s, daemon_pid 28181, 269.6 new PIDs/s; sampled 261.2/s; 164030 libproc polls; no sampled daemon children. Classified lower bounds: gone-before-seen 154.8/s, other 106.4/s. Statusline 0.0/s; Claude display-hook 0.0/s and stop-hook 0.5/s. This busy shared-machine sampler is not a CPU-isolated workload, and machine-wide activity is not attributed to this PR.

Proof

- just pr-freeze 306: FINAL, exact full head above, clean detached tree, CI 5/5.
- GitHub Actions run 44850296377, successful rust-test job 136679814322, attempt 1, head verified by API.
- Successful-job upload identifies junit-linux artifact ID 14685057196; downloaded by ID, not name. Its JUnit confirms ten selected tests passed: the two spawn-site tests; native-model selection; pending OMP model switch; repeated/concurrent warm reads; cancelled-read cursor preservation; compact footer fixtures; ambiguous-footer refusal; Claude-prefix resolution; corpus manifest consistency. These are test outcomes, not performance timings.
- CI command cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --profile ci: passed. CI doctests passed. Linux CI is not a macOS runtime-cost measurement.
- git diff --check: passed. No source edits, dependency installs/symlinks, local builds, canaries, bounce, seat closures or process kills. harness boot reported ready:false because vitest is absent; under C25, local TS/full harness gates were not run and are not represented as passing. Exact-head CI is the review proof.

Non-blocking notes owed

- Keep the cost wording explicit that a parsable OMP footer incurs the catalog charge even when native supplies the accepted model. The observed canary rate, not total seats or a polling interval, is its rate denominator.
- The authorized deploy owner must take the same PID/start/commit, per-op, CPU/RSS and machine receipts after deployment, and exercise an owned throwaway canary if measuring the active path. PR #306 is not deployed; no AFTER or live native/catalog latency measurement is claimed here.

Harness feedback / magicWand

A read-only cost-receipt command should capture both ping samples, monotonic interval, same-process identity, reconciled by-op deltas, per-route denominators, CPU/RSS and the separately labelled machine window. This review assembled those mechanically in session artifacts rather than altering the read-only worktree. Also distinguish "chosen source native" from "catalog invoked" in canary evidence; a populated native model does not prove that the footer/catalog work was skipped.
